skill.name: github-multi-repo
skill.description: Coordinates GitHub repositories, dependency updates, shared documentation, architecture standards, testing, and pull requests through Claude Flow workflows.
skill.summary: Guide multi-repository discovery, synchronization, testing, architecture, and coordinated GitHub changes.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, template delimiters, documentation links, and expected webhook secret access. Confirmed risks involve predictable shared temporary paths and unisolated npm execution. Broad multi-repository writes also lack explicit approval gates.

remediation.issue: Repository package and test scripts run with the agent environment.
remediation.suggestion: Use isolated containers, minimal tokens, repository allowlists, and restricted environment variables. Disable lifecycle scripts when they are unnecessary.

remediation.issue: Workflows reuse predictable files and directories under shared /tmp.
remediation.suggestion: Create private temporary directories with mktemp, quote every path, stop after clone failures, verify ownership, and remove temporary data with traps.

remediation.issue: Bulk GitHub mutations proceed without an explicit approval checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry runs and change summaries. Require user confirmation before API writes, dependency changes, commits, pushes, or pull request creation.

content.value_statement: Multi-repository changes are difficult to coordinate and validate consistently. This skill guides discovery, synchronization, testing, architecture standards, and pull request workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides repository discovery with GitHub CLI filters and dependency inspection.
Coordinates dependency and package version updates across repository groups.
Synchronizes documentation, workflows, and repository templates.
Defines cross-repository testing, security patching, and pull request flows.
Models swarm roles, synchronization strategies, monitoring, and architecture reporting.
limitations: The skill provides workflow instructions, not a standalone implementation.
GitHub CLI, jq, npm, Claude Flow, and authenticated repository access are required.
Examples use placeholder organizations, repositories, paths, and service endpoints.
Bulk commands can execute repository scripts and modify remote repositories.

use_cases.title: Align service dependencies
use_cases.description: Discover services, update shared dependencies, run tests, and prepare coordinated pull requests.

use_cases.title: Standardize repository architecture
use_cases.description: Review repository structures and apply common templates, workflows, and documentation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate security patches
use_cases.description: Scan selected repositories, identify vulnerable packages, test fixes, and track patch pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Discover repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: List repositories in {organization} matching {criteria}. Summarize languages, topics, and package dependencies. Do not modify anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only repository inventory.

prompt_templates.title: Plan dependency alignment
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare {package} versions across {repositories}. Propose an update order, compatibility checks, test commands, and rollback points.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Review CI workflows in {repositories}. Propose a shared template and repository-specific exceptions. Show changes before requesting approval.

prompt_templates.title: Orchestrate a phased migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan migration of {feature} across {repositories}. Map dependencies, execution waves, approval gates, tests, observability, rollback, and final reporting.

output_examples.input: Compare TypeScript versions across frontend, backend, and shared repositories.
output: Frontend uses version 5.4; backend uses 5.3; shared uses 5.4.
Update backend first, run unit tests, then run cross-repository integration tests.
Prepare one reviewed pull request per repository.

output_examples.input: Plan a security patch across twelve Node.js services.
output: Inventory completed for twelve selected repositories.
Patch in three dependency-aware waves with approval before each write phase.
Record test results, failures, and rollback instructions for every service.

output_examples.output: The report compares directory structure, CI workflows, documentation, ownership, and shared configuration, then prioritizes standardization changes.

best_practices: Start with read-only discovery and an explicit repository allowlist.
Use minimal GitHub permissions, isolated execution, and private temporary directories.
Require approval before remote writes and preserve test and rollback evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not run package scripts from unknown repositories on the host.
Do not use organization-wide wildcards for mutation without reviewing the resolved list.
Do not reuse predictable shared temporary files or continue after clone failures.

faq.question: Does this skill modify repositories automatically?
faq.answer: Its examples include branches, commits, file updates, pushes, and pull requests. Review the plan and approve writes before execution.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: Examples use GitHub CLI, jq, npm, Claude Flow, and authenticated GitHub access.

faq.question: Can it work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, when the active GitHub credentials can access every selected repository and operation.

faq.question: Does it support monorepos?
faq.answer: It discusses monorepo structures and migration planning, but focuses mainly on coordination across separate repositories.

faq.question: How should credentials be configured?
faq.answer: Use short-lived tokens with the minimum repository permissions. Keep secrets outside prompts, logs, and generated reports.

faq.question: How are failed updates handled?
faq.answer: The examples use tests and issue comments, but production use needs explicit rollback, cleanup, retries, and failure isolation.
